title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s go-to-market assets for sales and pre-sales: concise positioning and messaging, competitive battle cards, recommended pitch deck structure, pricing guidance and objections, two representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this document as the canonical reference for customer-facing engagements and handoffs to solutions engineering.

Audience:
- AEs, SDRs, Solutions Engineers, Partner PMs, and Sales Leadership.

Key takeaways:
- Position Redwood as a production-first inference platform that optimizes latency, cost, and reliability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Emphasize unified operational experience, predictable economics (Dedicated) and compliance readiness (Private).
- Equip reps with targeted objection responses, competitor differentiators, and measurable customer outcomes.

1. Positioning & Messaging (Elevator + 3 personas)

Elevator pitch (30s):
Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, production-grade LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — helping engineering teams reduce latency and per-token cost while maintaining model quality and compliance.

Core value pillars (one-liners):
- Production performance: GPU-optimized serving runtime with batching, KV caching, and kernel selection for consistent latency.
- Cost predictability: Dedicated capacity and Optimize toolkit that drive measurable unit cost reductions.
- Operational continuity: Same API, rollout controls, and observability across hosted, dedicated, and private modes.

Persona messaging
- ML Engineer: "Ship reliably — consistent serving primitives, model versioning, and deterministic performance across environments."
- Platform/Infra Lead: "Standardize inference across teams with contracts for capacity, SLAs, and cost controls."
- Product/PM: "Deliver rich LLM features with predictable latency and unit economics, plus guardrails for quality regressions."

Proof points (talk track bullets):
- Customers report 20–40% reduction in per-token inference cost after model/quantization recommendations.
- Native KV/prefix caching can reduce tail latency by up to 35% for chat workloads.
- Dedicated customers get SLA-backed 99.9% uptime and reserved throughput guarantees.

2. Competitive Briefs (short list + battle card highlights)

Top competitor categories: Managed LLM APIs, Cloud provider managed endpoints, Self-hosted inference runtimes.

Competitor: Major Managed LLM API (example: MegaAPI)
- Strengths: Broad model catalog, simple dev experience for prototyping.
- Weaknesses: Limited control over latency and cost at scale; fewer private deployment options.
- Redwood differentiator: Predictable SLOs, Dedicated capacity, and cost optimization toolkit for production workloads.

Competitor: Cloud Provider Endpoints (example: BigCloud ML Endpoints)
- Strengths: Deep cloud integration, enterprise contracts.
- Weaknesses: Fragmented API surface and higher unit costs at scale; slower kernel-level inference optimizations.
- Redwood differentiator: Single API across hosted/dedicated/private with optimized serving runtime and transparent performance profiles.

Competitor: Self-hosted Inference Stack (open-source runtimes + infra)
- Strengths: Maximum control, potentially lower infra cost if operated well.
- Weaknesses: High operational burden, slow MTTD/MTTR, lack of standard tooling for rollouts and evals.
- Redwood differentiator: Lower ops burden + production controls (canary, A/B, fallbacks) and rapid onboarding.

Battle card: Typical objections and counters
- "We can run this ourselves and save money." -> "Possibly, but hidden costs (ops headcount, downtime, model-tuning/time-to-market) often exceed savings. We provide measurable cost reduction levers and SLAs so product teams ship faster with predictable economics."
- "How do you compare on latency to X?" -> "We publish model+hardware profiles and suggest quantization/batch settings per workload. We also support dedicated GPU pools with reserved throughput for tail-sensitive applications."

3. Pitch Deck: Recommended Slide Flow (10–12 slides)

1) Title + 1-line positioning and logo
2) Customer problem: examples (latency spikes, cost variance, compliance overhead)
3) Why existing options fail (managed APIs/cloud endpoints/self-hosting)
4) The Redwood solution at a glance (hosted, dedicated, private)
5) How it works: runtime + smart routing + caching + deployment abstraction (one-paragraph diagram)
6) Key differentiators and proof points (metrics + quotes)
7) Demo summary / runbook for PoC
8) Pricing and commitment options (high-level)
9) Security & compliance summary (certs, KMS, audit logs)
10) Case study(s) with metrics (reduction in latency, cost, time-to-launch)
11) Next steps & recommended PoC scope
12) Appendix: integration checklist & SSO/KMS details

Demo checklist for SEs (pre-demo)
- Confirm demo dataset size and target latency SLO
- Pre-select model variant and quantization profile (recommend one conservative and one aggressive)
- Prepare a 5–7 minute live example and a fallback recorded run for flaky infra

4. Pricing Guidance (structure + negotiation playbook)

Pricing model overview (customer-facing):
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token generation + per-embedding unit).
- Dedicated: Reserved capacity contracts (monthly/annual commits) priced by GPU type and reserved throughput.
- Private: Platform license + support tier; optional on-prem packaging and professional services for integration.

Representative pricing tiers (for sales conversations, non-public):
- Developer Tier (Hosted): pay-as-you-go, low commitment, higher unit price — best for prototyping and early-stage apps.
- Growth / Business Tier (Hosted or Dedicated burst): committed monthly spend with discounts and access to Optimize toolkit.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: annual commitment with reserved throughput, advanced observability retention, and enterprise SLAs.

Negotiation levers for AEs
- Commitment length (12 vs 36 months) impacts discounting bands.
- Feature add-ons (extended observability retention, dedicated support) can be used in lieu of deeper unit discounts.
- Professional services for Private deployments are quoted separately; bundle to accelerate PoC.

Price objection scripts
- "Too expensive" -> "Let's break down total cost of ownership: unit inference cost + downtime/ops cost + time-to-market. Our Optimize recommendations often reduce the per-token cost materially and pay back commitments within months for production workloads."
- "We need a predictable monthly bill" -> "Dedicated capacity provides reserved throughput and predictable monthly cost with SLA coverage for tail-sensitive apps."

5. Case Studies (two anonymized examples with metrics)

Case study: E-Commerce Conversational Search (RetailCo, anonymized)
- Problem: Intermittent latency spikes and unpredictable inference cost during peak campaigns.
- Redwood solution: Migrated to Dedicated pools with KV prefix caching and model quantization recommendations; implemented canary rollouts for a new reranker.
- Outcome: 30% reduction in average latency, 27% reduction in per-session inference cost, zero production regressions during peak campaign.
- Timeline & ownership: Proof-of-concept (2 weeks), Production rollout (4 weeks), SE owner: Marco R.

Case study: Healthcare Triage Assistant (HealthSys, anonymized)
- Problem: Strict data residency and audit requirements prevented hosted APIs.
- Redwood solution: Private deployment with customer-managed VPC, KMS integration, and audit logging enabled.
- Outcome: Compliant deployment within 8 weeks, 99.9% uptime SLA, and measurable improvement in triage throughput (25% faster decisions).
- Timeline & ownership: On-prem engagement (8–12 weeks), PM lead: Priya S.

6. Security FAQ for Prospects (concise Q/A)

Q: Where does customer data reside?
A: By default hosted customers in region-based cloud tenancy; Dedicated and Private deployments allow data residency controls. We document region and retention options during onboarding.

Q: How is encryption handled?
A: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption using cloud KMS for hosted and Dedicated. Private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and access controls?
A: Yes — token-level audit logging, RBAC via SSO/OIDC, and per-route access policies. Audit log retention is configurable as an add-on.

Q: What compliance certifications do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 readiness artifacts; Private deployments make controlled evidence available during contract negotiation.

Q: How do you handle model/exposure risks (prompt leakage, data used for training)?
A: We support opt-out of data usage for model training for enterprise contracts, per-route redaction and masking hooks, and a recommended policy for prompt sanitization and tokenization.

7. Sales Playbook: Discovery and Objection Handling (scripts & checklists)

Discovery questions (prioritized):
1) What are your top 3 latency or cost pain points for LLM features?
2) What throughput / concurrency targets must you meet?
3) Are there data residency, audit, or compliance constraints?
4) What models or model families do you currently evaluate?
5) What is your ops team’s tolerance for running custom infra vs managed services?

Objection handling snippets
- "We already use X-managed API" -> "Understood — can you share your 90th/95th percentile latency and per-token cost? We can run a no-risk pilot and show delta with identical workload and model family."
- "We need to keep everything on-prem" -> "We support Private deployments and an on-prem package; let's scope network and storage requirements and propose a phased PoC."

8. PoC / Pilot recommended scope (4-week template)

Week 0: Kickoff, discovery, access and dataset handoff
Week 1: Baseline measurements on current stack; choose model variant and telemetry plan
Week 2: Deploy and validate on Redwood (hosted or dedicated trial); run load tests and annotate results
Week 3: Optimize quantization/batching and run A/B with production traffic sample
Week 4: Review results, produce ROI report, propose rollout plan and contract options

Deliverables:
- Latency and cost baseline report
- Recommended config (batching, quantization, caching)
- ROI and pricing proposal

9. Ownership, escalation, and handoffs

Primary owners:
- GTM: AE and Solutions Engineering for pre-sales and PoC
- Customer Success: Post-sale onboarding and SLA monitoring
- Product: Maintains pitch deck and product differentiation narrative

Escalation path:
1) SE -> Sales Engineering team lead
2) SE lead -> Enterprise Solutions Architect (for infra/security)
3) Enterprise Solutions Architect -> Product/SRE for runtime issues

10. Appendix: Integration checklist & recommended docs

Integration checklist (minimum):
- SSO/OIDC configured
- KMS integration plan (hosted vs customer-managed)
- Network/firewall rules for Private deployments
- Logging and telemetry endpoints confirmed
